plain_english_title: How VA's Secondary Service Connection & Aggravation Regulation (38 C.F.R. § 3.310) Evolved Over Time
what_this_means: This reference tracks the exact wording of 38 C.F.R. § 3.310 from 1979 to today. Originally focused on conditions proximately caused by a service-connected disability (plus heart disease after certain lower-limb amputations), the regulation expanded over four eras: adding tobacco cross-references in May 2001, formally codifying secondary aggravation and baseline-deduction rules in October 2006 following Allen v. Brown and Allen v. Principi, and adding five presumptive secondary illnesses linked to Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) effective January 16, 2014.
record_clues: A secondary claim denial issued before or after October 10, 2006 that considered only whether a service-connected disability 'caused' a non-service-connected condition without evaluating whether it 'aggravated' that condition.

A denial of liver, gastrointestinal, nerve, or heart complications resulting from alcohol or substance use that began as self-medication for service-connected PTSD, depression, or chronic pain (governed by Allen v. Principi and 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.301(d) and 3.310(a)–(b)).

A service-connected Traumatic Brain Injury accompanied by Parkinsonism, unprovoked seizures, certain dementias, depression, or pituitary hormone deficiency diagnosed on or after January 16, 2014 (§ 3.310(d)).
A service-connected amputation at or above one knee—or at or above both ankles—accompanied by ischemic heart disease or hypertension (§ 3.310(c)).
important_cautions: Exact amendment dates govern historical reviews: VA codified § 3.310(b) secondary aggravation effective October 10, 2006 (published September 7, 2006 at 71 FR 52744) and added § 3.310(d) TBI secondary presumptions effective January 16, 2014 (published December 17, 2013 at 78 FR 76196).

Missing a time window or severity threshold in § 3.310(d)(1) for a post-TBI condition does NOT bar a Veteran from establishing direct secondary causation or aggravation with a medical nexus opinion under § 3.310(a), (b), and (d)(2).

Tobacco limits apply differently depending on how smoking started: 38 U.S.C. § 1103 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.300(c) bar claims based on nicotine dependence starting in service, whereas secondary claims remain permitted when an already service-connected condition proximately caused post-service tobacco dependence and resulting disease.

Do not treat unfinalized or rescinded rules as active law: RIN 2900-AQ72 (sleep apnea) remains a proposed rule that is not enacted, and the February 17, 2026 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712). Also remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)'s limit of one final merits CUE decision per prior Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Which version of 38 C.F.R. § 3.310 was in force on the date of my prior rating decision, and did VA evaluate both causation (§ 3.310(a)) and aggravation (§ 3.310(b))?

If my secondary condition involves substance use or weight gain triggered by a service-connected mental or orthopedic condition, how do Allen v. Principi and VAOPGCPREC 1-2017 apply to an open or Supplemental Claim?

If I have a service-connected TBI and developed depression, seizures, Parkinsonism, hormone changes, or cognitive decline outside the § 3.310(d)(1) presumptive time windows, can we still submit a medical nexus opinion under § 3.310(d)(2)?
How does VA establish my pre-aggravation baseline under § 3.310(b) so that only the pre-existing degree is deducted?
